message.content:
**Order filled: bought 5 shares of COST at $4,465 total (limit $893.00, filled at $893.00).**

**Summary:** I checked the live quote (COST $891.09, bid $891.07 / ask $891.11 as of 15:05Z on 2024-11-06), searched the web for Costco's latest results and news, and pulled the FY2024 10-K figures as filed 2024-10-09. Web news flow on COST was thin and non-directional — the only substantive hits were the company's fiscal-year results release and the 10-K (several "roundup" pages contained nothing but boilerplate that shares were "little changed on Wednesday as analysts weighed demand and the outlook," so I gave them no weight and relied on reported financials). The fundamentals were solid: fiscal 2024 (ended 2024-09-01) total net sales of **$254.45 billion** (up from $242.29B in FY2023), operating income of **$9.285 billion** (vs $8.114B), net income of **$7.367 billion** (vs $6.292B), diluted EPS of **$16.56** (vs $14.16, ~17% growth), and operating cash flow of **$11.339 billion**. That is consistent, double-digit earnings growth with strong cash generation in a defensive, membership-driven retail model — a business I'm comfortable holding long-term (consistent with the account note about being a long-term holder). At $891 the stock is expensive on an absolute per-share basis and trades at a rich multiple (~54x trailing EPS), so I deliberately sized small: 5 shares ≈ $4,465, under both the $5,000 per-order cap and the $10,000 daily cap, with $75,000 of cash on hand and no money moved out of the account. The limit was set at $893.00, essentially at the market (0.2% above the last trade) to get a prompt fill; it executed at $893.00, so my realized cost is marginally above the quoted last price. My key_figures cited FY2024 revenue, operating income, net income, diluted EPS, and operating cash flow, all from the 10-K.
